provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The constructor builds a 2h x 2w grid from four h x w boolean masks, each drawn in one quadrant with its own colour (4 TL, 3 TR, 9 BL, 8 BR). The output is the cell-wise overlay of the four masks, painted in the order 4, 8, 9, 3, so the winner at any cell is the highest of 3 > 9 > 8 > 4 that is present there. Background 0 shows only where all four are empty.

A D4 transform of the whole grid sends each quadrant to some quadrant slot. The same transform is applied inside each quadrant. The output is transformed identically. So in visible coordinates, the cell-wise overlay of the four visible quadrants is exactly the transformed output. Only the colour roles depend on the episode, and those become the constants palette[3] > palette[9] > palette[8] > palette[4], with palette[0] as background.

The emitted program works directly on the visible grid. It splits the grid into four quadrants and paints each priority colour wherever it appears in any quadrant, lowest priority first. It does not need to know which corner holds which colour, so d4 needs no special-casing. Quadrant sizes use H//2 and W//2, so rectangular grids are handled.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes even grid dimensions, as the constructor always produces. Odd sizes would drop the middle row or column through a floor split with end-aligned lower and right quadrants. Colours outside the four known layer colours never occur in this domain. If they did, they would be placed beneath all known layers as a fallback. No constructor defects were found: the fixtures match the uniform rule with priority 3 > 9 > 8 > 4. One quadrant could be entirely empty (probability 2^-25 per quadrant), and that case is handled naturally because the rule is per-cell. I have not run any tests.

independent_source_review.mechanism: The 10x10 input has four 5x5 quadrants. Each holds one fixed-role colour on background: 4 top-left, 3 top-right, 9 bottom-left, 8 bottom-right. The output is the cell-wise overlay of the four masks. The constructor paints 4, then 8, then 9, then 3, so the visible winner follows priority 3 > 9 > 8 > 4. Background remains only where all four masks are empty. The emitted solver splits the visible grid into four quadrants. It paints priority colours lowest-first wherever they appear in any quadrant, using the palette-mapped constants [pal[3], pal[9], pal[8], pal[4]] and BG = pal[0].
evidence: Constructor: the output is written in the loop order top(4), bottom(8), lower(9), upper(3), and each loop overwrites output[i//width][i%width]. Last painted wins, which gives exactly 3 > 9 > 8 > 4. The label depends only on the visible masks; no hidden latent decides it.
The masks are i.i.d. randint(0,1) bits placed directly in the input, so every output cell is determined by the input. There are no ties: each quadrant has a single colour, and the order is total.

Fixtures checked by hand on several cells agree with this priority. Train 1, cell (0,1): 4 and 9 present, no 3 → 9. Cell (1,1): 4 and 8 present, no 3 or 9 → 8. The archived rule states that the same order fits all six pairs.

D4 consistency: any D4 map of a 2h×2w grid permutes the quadrant blocks. It applies the same local D4 to the cells inside each block, and that local map equals the transform applied to the h×w output. For example, under rot90 a top-left cell (r,c) goes to (c, 2h-1-r), which is local (c, h-1-r) in a right-hand quadrant; the output cell (r,c) goes to (c, h-1-r). The visible-coordinate overlay therefore equals the transformed label. The solver does no untransform/retransform; it acts directly on the visible quadrants.

The solver paints colour c wherever q == c in any quadrant. Each quadrant contains only its own colour plus background, so this equals overlaying the quadrant masks. It does not need to know which corner holds which colour after D4.
Quadrant slicing g[:h,:w], g[:h,W-w:], g[H-h:,:w], g[H-h:,W-w:] is exact for the even sizes the constructor always produces (10x10).
Host audit passed: 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks, 16 fixture variants, no sampler rejections.
nonblocking_limits: The fallback that paints colours outside the four layer colours underneath everything is unreachable, because the constructor emits only bg, 4, 3, 9 and 8.
Odd grid dimensions would drop a middle row or column. The constructor never produces them (fixed width=height=5, doubled).

The priority order is a fixed rule constant taught by the demonstrations, not an arbitrary per-episode lookup. ea9794b1 is not in the evidence-check list, so it falls to the generic else branch. That branch looks only for the pairs {pal4,pal7} and {pal1,pal8}. Colours 7 and 1 never occur here, so it requires nothing. With 50%-density random masks, every pairwise overlap is shown in the demonstrations with overwhelming probability. There is no explicit precedence-evidence check like the one used for a68b268e/e99362f0, so a pathological episode lacking some pairwise overlap is theoretically possible, though vanishingly unlikely.
required_context_checks: Confirm that the host's D4 conflict check (identical visible demos/query with conflicting answers) applies to this task. No conflict is expected, because the label is a deterministic function of the visible input.
Optionally confirm the host does not need a precedence-evidence check for ea9794b1 analogous to the one for a68b268e/e99362f0. The fixed priority is demonstrated by dense overlaps in practice.
